comparison: Perfect agreement on proliferation findings (C1, C28-C37). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing with adequate statistical support, appropriate controls, and multiple markers (Ki67, BrdU). Reviewers did not challenge these core findings.

Agreement on dorsal-ventral dissociation (C39-C40, C57-C60). Both evaluations accept the regional specificity findings and the mRNA-protein dissociation in ventral DG. Reviewers did not challenge these experimental results.

Agreement on BLA lesion findings (C3, C43-C45). Both evaluations accept the experimental evidence for BLA-independence of stress-induced proliferation. OpenEval notes unilateral lesion limitation; reviewers requested contextual discussion but did not challenge results.

Disagreement on astrocytic FGF2 source (C2, C49-C52, C67). OpenEval finds multi-level evidence sufficient despite noting statistical concerns with C51. Peer reviewers expressed uncertainty, requesting additional in situ hybridization or immunohistochemistry to exclude culture contamination and strengthen in vivo astrocyte source claims.

Disagreement on FGF2 mechanism specificity (C4, C70-C74). OpenEval finds antibody neutralization experiments provide strong mechanistic evidence with appropriate specificity controls. Peer reviewers expressed uncertainty about antibody specificity to FGF2 versus other FGF family members and requested absolute rather than relative FGF2 levels.

Disagreement on inverted-U framework (C7, C27, C93, C96-C97). OpenEval rates as uncertain due to lack of systematic dose-response data and speculative language. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed this as a key contribution, stating it reveals 'a new domain of the inverse-U phenomenon' and should be highlighted in the Introduction.

Agreement on in vitro NPC findings (C46-C47). Both evaluations accept that CORT does not directly affect NPCs while FGF2 does. Reviewers' concerns about astrocyte cultures relate to interpretation of the communication mechanism rather than these basic observations.

Partial disagreement on fear extinction findings (C5, C76-C78). OpenEval finds behavioral evidence well-documented with appropriate controls and temporal design. Peer reviewers did not challenge the data quality but expressed uncertainty about integration, stating these findings 'feel like they belong in a different paper.'

Overlapping evaluation of neuronal activation (C6, C81). OpenEval supports the cellular evidence linking behavior to cfos activation in DCX+ cells, noting correlative nature. Peer reviewers' uncertainty about fear extinction data integration (R5) extends to these activation findings as part of the behavioral story.

Agreement on cell survival and differentiation null results (C79-C80). Both evaluations accept these findings without challenge. OpenEval notes these support enhanced recruitment interpretation; reviewers did not question these data.

OpenEval evaluated habituation effects (C38, C102-C104) as supported methodological findings that could explain literature discrepancies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, suggesting reviewers did not specifically comment on these claims.

OpenEval evaluated comprehensive growth factor screening (C53-C65) as well-supported with appropriate statistical analyses and controls. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, suggesting reviewers did not challenge this broad screening approach.

OpenEval evaluated mechanistic framework claims (C82-C85) as supported by citations, noting authors inferred rather than directly demonstrated GR translocation and FGF2 transcriptional regulation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rated functional interpretation claims (C108-C110) as uncertain due to correlative nature and lack of causal manipulation experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific interpretive claims.

OpenEval evaluated literature summary claims (C22-C26) as accurately representing prior work with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though reviewers did request additional BLA discussion in Introduction.
OpenEval evaluated citations justifying temporal design (C75, C86-C89) as well-supported and providing strong rationale for 2-week behavioral timepoint. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluated comparative and translational literature citations (C91-C92, C94-C95, C105, C107) as accurately cited and strengthening translational relevance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these relate to inverted-U framework endorsed by reviewers in R6.
